title: Limits and Continuity
summary: lim x→a f(x) = L means f(x) gets as close to L as we like when x is close to (but not equal to) a. The limit exists only if the left-hand and right-hand limits are equal.
Methods: direct substitution; factorise and cancel for 0/0 forms; rationalise expressions with square roots; use standard limits.

lim x→a (xⁿ − aⁿ)/(x − a) = naⁿ⁻¹. lim x→0 sin x/x = 1 (x in radians), so lim x→0 sin kx/x = k. lim x→0 (1 − cos x)/x² = ½. lim x→0 (eˣ − 1)/x = 1, so lim x→0 (e^(kx) − 1)/x = k. lim x→0 log(1 + x)/x = 1.
lim x→3 |x − 3|/(x − 3) does not exist: the left limit is −1 and the right limit is +1.

f is continuous at x = a if f(a) is defined and lim x→a f(x) = f(a), i.e. LHL = RHL = f(a). Polynomials, sin x, cos x, eˣ and |x| are continuous everywhere. To find an unknown constant, equate the limit to the value at the point.

Right-hand limit = 1, left-hand limit = −1. They differ, so the limit does not exist.

mcq: continuous at all points of R
objective: True or False: (a) f(x) = 1 (x ≠ 0), 2 (x = 0) is continuous at x = 0. (b) f(x) = |x| is continuous at all points of R.

(a) False — the limit at 0 is 1 but f(0) = 2.
(b) True.

1 − cos x = 2 sin²(x/2).
2 sin²(x/2)/x² = ½[sin(x/2)/(x/2)]² → ½ × 1 = ½.

tan²x = sin²x/cos²x = (1 − cos x)(1 + cos x)/cos²x.
(1 + cos x)cos²x/[(1 − cos x)(1 + cos x)] = cos²x/(1 − cos x) → 1/(1 + 1) = ½.

sa: f(x) = (1 − cos 4x)/x² for x < 0, a for x = 0, √x/(√(16 + √x) − 4) for x > 0. If f is continuous at 0, find a.

LHL: 1 − cos 4x = 2 sin²2x ⇒ 2 sin²2x/x² = 8[sin 2x/(2x)]² → 8.
RHL: rationalise: √x(√(16 + √x) + 4)/(16 + √x − 16) = √(16 + √x) + 4 → 4 + 4 = 8.
Continuity: a = 8.
